note: The opening line on the start sheet (top-level design 16). It changes by itself: the first three visits show lines 1 to 3, then a weighted pick, never the same twice running, preferring what this person has not opened. A line whose `needs` are not all built is held back. `opens` says what Show me does: a screen at system scale, a world screen (on the selected world, else the first), a desk, a dialog, a door of the sheet, or a link. Packs may add lines later. `atlas` is the sheet's "What it can do" list: ten verbs, each opening the real thing (tours come with top-level step 5).

lines.headline: Your sci-fi campaign, on real physics.
lines.sentence: Build the systems your players fly through, then share a screen that shows only what they have found.

lines.headline: A universe that works out its own physics.
lines.sentence: Go anywhere, at any time, and ask why.

lines.headline: Come for the role-playing game. Leave with the astrophysics.
lines.sentence: Every number opens to the physics behind it, and to the paper behind that.

lines.headline: Players see only what they have scanned.
lines.sentence: You hold the whole chart. Their screen fills in as they explore.

lines.headline: How long to Mars, and will the crew survive it?
lines.sentence: Courses compared by fuel, time, radiation dose and what they pass on the way.

lines.headline: What does the sky look like from there?
lines.sentence: Stand on any world and look up, through eyes, binoculars or a telescope.

lines.headline: Find tonight's story.
lines.sentence: Ask for the places worth a session: a world about to lose its oceans, a moon nobody has surveyed.

lines.headline: Dress the bridge.
lines.sentence: Give players a green-screen terminal, a glass cockpit or a paper chart, all showing the same system.

lines.headline: A Traveller sector, turned into real systems.
lines.sentence: Import the codes and get worlds whose physics agrees with them, with the ones that cannot flagged.

lines.headline: Run an empire game with real fog of war.
lines.sentence: Each side sees only what it has discovered, on its own screen.

lines.headline: Give the pirates something to do.
lines.sentence: Patrols, raiders and drones carry on by their own rules while the players are elsewhere.

lines.headline: The same universe on every screen at the table.
lines.sentence: No server holds your campaign. Each device works out the same result from the same seed.

lines.headline: Build a world. Then find out what it does.
lines.sentence: Set a mass and an orbit. The air, the oceans and the seasons follow.

lines.headline: No excuse for bad physics.
lines.sentence: Make your setting as strange as you like. Where it breaks the rules, it says so and tells you why.

lines.headline: The universe is weirder than anything you would invent.
lines.sentence: Tar seas, moons heated from inside, stars that swallow their planets. They turn up without being asked.

lines.headline: Grow a solar system from a cloud of gas.
lines.sentence: Watch the worlds form, migrate and collide, with every stage of the history kept.

lines.headline: Find a home.
lines.sentence: Ask for an ocean world with one moon and a quiet star, and be shown where one could be.

lines.headline: Design a planet nobody has thought of.
lines.sentence: Place it on the class chart and see what kind of world that combination makes.

lines.headline: Writing a novel? Check the voyage.
lines.sentence: How long it takes, what it costs in fuel, and what the crew sees on arrival.

lines.headline: Borrow someone else's galaxy.
lines.sentence: Open a campaign from the Explorers library, or take one world from it for your own.

lines.headline: Bring your old maps.
lines.sentence: Saves from version 3, Universe Sandbox and SpaceEngine come in with a report of what changed.

lines.headline: Ten billion years on one slider.
lines.sentence: Age the Sun and watch what happens to Earth.

lines.headline: Cut a planet in half.
lines.sentence: Core, mantle, crust, ocean and air, each with the reason it is there.

lines.headline: See it in X-rays.
lines.sentence: Switch the light you look in and the same star becomes a different object.

lines.headline: Why is this planet here at all?
lines.sentence: Follow one world back through its history to the dust it formed from.

lines.headline: Is anything alive down there?
lines.sentence: How a living world got its air, and what lives on what.

lines.headline: How big is it, really?
lines.sentence: Put any worlds and stars side by side at true scale.

lines.headline: What if Jupiter were closer?
lines.sentence: Try it on a branch. Keep the result or throw it away.

lines.headline: Could we have found this planet from Earth?
lines.sentence: Try the real methods: the dip as it crosses its star, the wobble it gives it.

lines.headline: Read a star's light.
lines.sentence: A spectrum of anything, with the lines labelled and what they tell you.

lines.headline: Change the physics.
lines.sentence: Each rule is a small diagram you can open, edit and trace to its source.

lines.headline: Teach a class with it.
lines.sentence: Make a tour of saved places with your own captions, and hand out the link.

lines.headline: Settle an argument.
lines.sentence: What would Earth be like at the distance of Mars? Move it and see.

lines.headline: Just wander.
lines.sentence: There is always another system, and nobody has looked at most of them.

lines.headline: Break it.
lines.sentence: Every example can be wrecked and put back with one button.

lines.headline: Zoom out until galaxies are dots.
lines.sentence: From one world to the cosmic web, and back again.

lines.headline: Take its photograph.
lines.sentence: A world in true colour, drawn from its own air and ground.

lines.headline: Listen to a solar system.
lines.sentence: Orbits as sound, off until you ask for it.

lines.headline: Ask it anything.
lines.sentence: Tars answers from the physics in front of you, and says where the answer came from.

lines.headline: Tell it what you want built.
lines.sentence: Describe a screen, a lens or a rule in a sentence and Orac drafts it for you to check.

lines.headline: Build your own game on it.
lines.sentence: The engine is open source and repeatable: the same seed gives the same universe on every device.

lines.headline: Need a starship screen for your film?
lines.sentence: Themed displays driven by a real system make convincing background screens.
